text:
Dylan Guenther has 12 points in 18 games, and 9 of them have come on the power play. That is the shape of his season so far: lethal with the man advantage, quiet at even strength. He has 3 points in his last ten games against 7.5 our numbers expected from his ice time and role, which makes this one of the bigger gaps in the league between what a player has done lately and what his chances say.

The chances are fine. He has 6.2 expected goals and is shooting a normal 13%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.2 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 92nd percentile, and Evolving-Hockey had most of his value coming from even-strength offense. That is exactly the part missing right now.

Our range has him around 34 goals and 67 points, below last season's 40 but well above his current pace. At 23, on more than 17 minutes a night, he is a cold month away from a hot one. We'd expect the even-strength goals to show up before long.
headline: Guenther is a power play weapon, for now
